title: I'm better than you.
summary: A Nietzschean rant on slave versus master morality, prompted by backlash to his 'reject mediocrity' video. NH argues that calling claims of superiority arrogant is slave morality: it vilifies excellence, lowers standards and breeds mediocrity. Lifters should take pride in being objectively better than the average man while staying hungry, then use solitude to build themselves and return to lift others up.
claims: Real humility is objectively assessing where you stand; saying 'I am strong' when you are strong is honesty, not arrogance
People who condemn claims of superiority are usually trying to feel better by reframing the superior as evil, i.e. slave morality
Lowering standards to protect feelings (participation trophy culture) devalues rewards and removes the incentive to work
Nietzsche's transvaluation of values: slaves who couldn't meet master morality redefined the strong as evil and the weak as good
He trained two hours in a 0 °C garage until his toes froze, while the average man skips sessions in a heated commercial gym; that makes him objectively superior on that score
Lifters should take pride in being better than the average man; without pride in self-improvement there is no reason to lift
When someone says they are better than you, treat it as an invitation to prove them wrong by improving
Friends who call your new healthy habits cringe are protecting their own comfort; keep going and widen the gap so they either follow or fall away
Hiding your accomplishments to spare others' feelings keeps them comfortable in mediocrity; instead tell them they can reach your level
The average man stays average by comparing himself to the average; he calls himself weak despite squatting four plates and pulling five because his standards are high
Master modesty: knowing you are better than some people while knowing you can still improve; constant self-deprecation is also slave morality
Use solitude as a tool to build a solid identity away from the crab bucket, then return to society to inspire others, not a permanent sigma grindset
